Q: Opinions on the rapid development of AI A:

for now I think the most anxious are the paper-pushers not the coders. I think everyone is equally anxious about the future because eventually AI and/or AI robots could eventually do every single job on the planet. (I'm unable to think of one it couldn't do if it keeps progressing at this pace...)

Currently AI is particularly bad at producing secure code, so maybe front-end is a tad more nervous. The backend secures and controls access, so less likely that a company would rely solely on AI to produce that code. Having said that, the frontend can also introduce vulnerabilities for it's users. (things like XSS, CSRF, etc...) Worse still, an AI agent architecting a frontend/backend system that relies on the front-end to secure access. Would an AI CEO allow itself to be full-stack engineer or would it place an ad, take interviews and hire a human?

Q: Is it possible to dismiss the DatePicker calendar when a date is tapped? A:

SwiftUI 2026

Another thing you can do, especially if you don't always want to change the date, is to have it dismiss when you stop hovering over it.

Include this at the start of the View struct:

@Environment(\.dismiss) private var dismiss

Then, on the DatePicker, add this:

.onHover { hovering in if !hovering { dismiss() } }

This works great if the DatePicker is presented in a Popover, but you can do something similar if your view is presented some other way.
